original_question: Are there plane billiards, other than ellipses, that possess rational caustics with two different values of the rotation numbers? Same question for outer billiards.
target_in_paper: Question 3.7 in §3.2.2, “Geometry of caustics, invariant surfaces, and commuting billiard maps.”
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s official formulation almost verbatim. It correctly identifies the planar inner-billiard setting, excludes ellipses, asks for coexistence of rational caustics with two distinct rotation numbers, and includes the parallel outer-billiard question.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, specify that a planar billiard here is the inner billiard in a strictly convex domain Ω ⊂ R^2 bounded by a smooth curve γ.
Define a p/q-rational caustic as an invariant circle of the billiard map consisting of periodic points with rotation number p/q.
Spell out that “two different values of the rotation numbers” means there exist two distinct rational numbers p1/q1 and p2/q2 with p1/q1 ≠ p2/q2; the paper does not fix which pair.

For the outer-billiard half, specify that the map is the outer billiard transformation of the exterior of a closed convex plane curve; the paper states the analogous question there without restating further notation.
Do not add analyticity, perturbative hypotheses, or a specific pair such as 1/2 and 1/3; those appear only in a nearby partial result, not in Question 3.7 itself.
There are no ambient-field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, operator-theoretic, or “for all sufficiently large m” conditions in this problem; the hidden assumptions are geometric instead.
refined_question: Let Ω ⊂ R^2 be a strictly convex planar billiard table with smooth boundary γ, and call a p/q-rational caustic an invariant circle of the billiard map consisting of periodic points with rotation number p/q. Does there exist a non-elliptic planar billiard table whose billiard map has p1/q1-rational and p2/q2-rational caustics for two distinct rational rotation numbers p1/q1 ≠ p2/q2? Likewise, does there exist an outer billiard on the exterior of a closed convex plane curve, other than the elliptic case, with rational caustics for two distinct rational rotation numbers?
justification: The draft is targeting exactly Question 3.7 in §3.2.2, p. 20. The only work needed is to import the local definitions supplied just before it and in the surrounding section: §3.2 defines the planar billiard table Ω ⊂ R^2 with smooth strictly convex boundary and explains what a caustic is, while §3.2.2 defines a p/q-rational caustic as an invariant circle made of periodic points with rotation number p/q. The outer-billiard side is also introduced earlier in §3.2 as the area-preserving transformation of the exterior of a closed convex plane curve. The paper does not present an equivalent reformulation of Question 3.7; instead it gives a weaker neighboring statement, Conjecture 3.8. The nearby remark about Kaloshin–Zhang concerns only a special analytic perturbative case (1/2 and 1/3 caustics), so that hypothesis should not be inserted into the refined question.
